review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped Mathlib for other convergence-in-measure notions. Only `TendstoInMeasure` itself and its users turned up, so there is no competing definition of the concept. The `tendstoInMeasure_iff_*` variants are useful named restatements and I didn't flag them. The one candidate is the hand-built strictly monotone extraction `seqTendstoAeSeq`. It reimplements `Filter.extraction_forall_of_eventually'`, which I checked in Order/Filter/AtTopBot/Basic.lean. A grep over the Mathlib source tree found no uses of these declarations outside this file. I also did not evaluate whether `seqTendstoAeSeq_spec`'s `max` construction has other uses. Whether the replacement compiles is untested. The `exists_seq_tendsto_ae` proof would need adjusting to use `φ` and its spec directly. The file also appears to have a stray second `end ExistsSeqTendstoAe` at line 347. The namespace opened at line 224 is already closed at line 262. This is probably a quirk of how the file was presented to me, and it is not relevant to this rubric.

findings.excerpt:
noncomputable def seqTendstoAeSeq (hfg : TendstoInMeasure μ f atTop g) : ℕ → ℕ
  | 0 => seqTendstoAeSeqAux hfg 0
  | n + 1 => max (seqTendstoAeSeqAux hfg (n + 1)) (seqTendstoAeSeq hfg n + 1)
findings.problem: The file builds its own strictly monotone extraction. It chooses thresholds `N n` with `Classical.choose`, then forces strict monotonicity through a recursive `max` definition. That takes two noncomputable defs plus three lemmas (`_succ`, `_spec`, `_strictMono`), all public API in a dedicated namespace. Mathlib already has this concept as `Filter.extraction_forall_of_eventually'`. From `∀ n, ∃ N, ∀ k ≥ N, P n k` it produces `∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ ∀ n, P n (φ n)`. `exists_nat_measure_lt_two_inv` already gives exactly that hypothesis with `P n k := μ {x | 2⁻¹ ^ n ≤ edist (f k x) (g x)} ≤ 2⁻¹ ^ n`. The only user of these declarations is `TendstoInMeasure.exists_seq_tendsto_ae`, in this file.
findings.proposed_change: Delete `seqTendstoAeSeqAux`, `seqTendstoAeSeq`, `seqTendstoAeSeq_succ`, `seqTendstoAeSeq_spec` and `seqTendstoAeSeq_strictMono`. Keep `exists_nat_measure_lt_two_inv`. In `exists_seq_tendsto_ae`, obtain `⟨ns, hns, hspec⟩ := extraction_forall_of_eventually' (exists_nat_measure_lt_two_inv hfg)`. Then use `hns` for `StrictMono` and `hspec k` in place of `seqTendstoAeSeq_spec hfg k (ns k) le_rfl` for `hμS_le`.
findings.benefit: About 35 lines of bespoke public API disappear. The subsequence construction now uses Mathlib's standard extraction lemma, so readers don't have to check a custom `max` recursion. The proof of `exists_seq_tendsto_ae` also gets shorter.

evidence.excerpt:
theorem extraction_forall_of_eventually' {P : ℕ → ℕ → Prop} (h : ∀ n, ∃ N, ∀ k ≥ N, P n k) :
    ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ ∀ n, P n (φ n)
